references.text: Call to praise from the waters above the heavens – a direct parallel to the waters above the firmament
God stretches out the heavens like a tent and sets the beams of his upper chambers on the waters
Wisdom was present when God established the dome of heaven and set boundaries for the sea
God has drawn a boundary over the surface of the waters, where light and darkness meet
God created the earth by his power and stretched out the heavens by his understanding; at his command the waters above the heavens roar
The heavens and the earth were formed from water and through water by God's word
By faith we understand that the world was created by God's word, so that what is visible came from what is invisible
Parallel creative act: God's separation of opposites (light/darkness and waters/waters) as the foundation for order.
Essential narrative and theological connection: The separation of the waters (1:7) creates the space that makes life along the dome possible (1:20).
Microcosmic parallel: God's ability to separate water from dry land (dew on the fleece) mirrors the macrocosmic separation in creation.
Theological parallel: God's control over the boundaries of the waters to create space (in creation) and a way (in the exodus).
Direct allusion to the cosmology of creation: Ezekiel's vision of the firmament (rakia) confirms and expands upon the structure established in Genesis 1:7.
